description: Only a JUnit 5 test class and a pretty-printed JaCoCo XML for the class it tests are pasted. There is no production source, no scope (diff / changed-file list) and no test results. JaCoCo shows partial coverage of com.acme.hr.leave.LeaveBalanceCalculator. The tool can report coverage numbers per class and line numbers from the XML, but cannot map <line nr> values to code, cannot list production methods from source and cannot decide which classes are in scope.
notes: No source paste: productionClasses is intentionally omitted. JaCoCo still names the class and its methods (<init>, entitlement, carryForward, prorate, balance) with descriptors and first lines; a tool may list those as "from coverage report" but cannot verify that a <line nr> is executable or show its code.
No scope paste: scope is intentionally omitted. The tool must say the changed-class scope is unknown and cannot claim that every changed class is covered.
No results paste: whether the tests passed is unknown.
Fully uncovered lines 27 and 36 and partial-branch lines 19, 26 and 35 are only meaningful together with the source, which was not provided; they should be reported as bare line numbers only.

The test is in the same package as the class under test, so com.acme.hr.leave.LeaveBalanceCalculatorTest -> com.acme.hr.leave.LeaveBalanceCalculator can be matched by naming convention to the JaCoCo class com/acme/hr/leave/LeaveBalanceCalculator.
A test method is literally named "balance", the same as the production method it calls.
The JaCoCo <init> at line 6 is the implicit default constructor (the class declaration line).
